summary: Backend regression suite for email-pipeline fixes (iteration 59). 15/15 tests passed. Verified: signup lowercases email, mixed-case login works (direct + legacy-fallback regex), /admin/email-health exposes postmark_token_present + send_failure_counts + recent_failures (existing fields preserved), /admin/email/diagnose returns found/user/recent_events/chat_throttle/recent_send_failures with case-insensitive fallback, missing-param 400 guard, admin-only 403 RBAC on both endpoints, suppression path skips Postmark and inserts email_send_failures row with reason_code='suppressed' (surfacing in /admin/email-health), and _bg_email_tasks strong-ref set exists in both routes/chat.py & routes/auth.py with schedule/discard lifecycle working.
critical_code_review_comments: utils/email.py send_password_reset_email() at line 449 in auth.py is awaited inline (not via _schedule_bg_email). If Postmark is slow this blocks the /auth/forgot-password response. Not a bug for correctness but worth noting for latency parity with the chat path.

routes/admin/events.py /admin/email/diagnose queries db.chat_email_throttle by 'to_email', but routes/chat.py writes throttle rows keyed by receiver_id/sender_id/property_id (no to_email field). The chat_throttle array will always be empty in diagnose output. Consider joining users→throttle by receiver_id, or storing to_email on write, so support can actually see whether recent chat throttling was blocking sends.

routes/admin/events.py diagnose fallback regex `^{email}$` does not escape regex metacharacters in the email (e.g. '.'), which is fine for '.' matching itself but a malformed input could throw. Low priority.
